features.name: Grouping events into issues, issue state
Event storage with retention and cold storage

workloadAssumptions: Ingest volume is bursty and far above what one Durable Object writer should absorb; events must not go through a workspace's write path.
Issue state (status, assignee, counts) is small and per project.

architecture.summary: A compatible rewrite that keeps raw events out of TapeDB: a Worker accepts Sentry envelopes, acknowledges after enqueuing to Queues, consumers group events and write issue rows to a TapeDB workspace per organization, raw events go through Basin Pipelines into R2 Iceberg tables for search and retention, and alerts go out through TapeDB webhooks or Queues.

components.responsibility: DSN check, size limits, enqueue, ack

components.name: Grouping consumer
components.responsibility: fingerprint, upsert issue rows in batches

components.name: Organization workspace
components.responsibility: orgs, projects, issues, assignments, alert rules; live issue lists

components.name: Event store
components.primitive: Basin Pipelines, R2 Iceberg, Basin SQL

capabilities.description: Acknowledge an event only once it is durably accepted
capabilities.candidate: Worker sends to Queues before responding
gaps: Verified in workerd with local Queues only; not run against deployed Queues.
Envelope parsing covers event items; attachments, sessions and transactions items are ignored.

capabilities.description: Rate limits and quotas per project
capabilities.candidate: Workers rate limiting binding plus counters

capabilities.description: Issue rows, status, assignment with live lists
capabilities.candidate: TapeDB models and live queries in a workspace per organization
gaps: Write throughput of one organization's workspace at ingest rate not benchmarked; the consumer writes one transaction per event.

capabilities.description: Fingerprinting compatible with Sentry SDK grouping
gaps: Simplified fingerprinting (explicit fingerprint, last exception type and value with numbers removed, or message); not compared against Sentry's grouping.

capabilities.candidate: Basin Pipelines into R2 Iceberg; Basin SQL
gaps: Basin SQL latency for interactive event lists not measured.
TapeDB is not an event store and is not used here.

capabilities.candidate: Iceberg partition expiry; TapeDB rows deleted by a scheduled job

capabilities.description: Organizations, teams, projects, DSN keys, membership
capabilities.candidate: TapeDB built-in auth with membership and a workspace per organization
gaps: DSN key lookup at the ingest edge needs a fast path outside the workspace (cache).

capabilities.description: Alerts on new or regressed issues
capabilities.candidate: TapeDB webhooks on issue rows into a Queues consumer
gaps: Webhook delivery is verified; alert rule evaluation is application code.

capabilities.candidate: Source maps in a Worker; native debug files not assessed
gaps: Native symbolication may exceed Worker CPU and memory limits.

risks.description: Writing raw events into a workspace would hit the single-writer limit.
risks.mitigation: Raw events never enter TapeDB; only batched issue upserts do.

risks.description: Event search through Basin SQL may be too slow for interactive views.
risks.mitigation: Measure before committing; keep the latest events per issue in the workspace.

risks.description: TapeDB's /v1/transact takes wire ops as they are and does not apply schema defaults; an insert missing a defaulted field is refused (invalid_op).
risks.mitigation: The consumer spells out every defaulted field; reported upstream as a documentation gap.

costAssumptions.assumption: About 3 operations per event before batching.
Event search billed per TB scanned.
Batched issue upserts; volume not modelled.

decisions.title: Keep raw events out of TapeDB
decisions.context: GlitchTip stores events in partitioned Postgres and cold Parquet.

options.name: Events in TapeDB workspaces
options.tradeoffs: One writer per organization; storage and rows billed per event.

options.name: Events in Basin; issues in TapeDB
options.tradeoffs: Two stores; each fits its workload.

decisions.choice: Events in Basin; issues in TapeDB
decisions.consequences: Event search goes to Basin SQL; issue lists stay live through TapeDB.

tests.description: Typed reads and writes in workerd and on staging
Live diffs keep order when rows move
Signed webhooks delivered in order with retries
Envelope accepted only after enqueue; unknown key refused; poison event retried, dead-lettered and recorded; siblings not held back
Issues grouped by fingerprint; counts summed from per-message tallies; a redelivered message counts once
